chunks.arabic_text: ٢٢ - عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُمَيْرِ بْنِ مَحْفُوظٍ الْبَلَوِيِّ، أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ، الْمِصْرِيُّ.

translations.en: 22 – ʿAbdullāh b. Muḥammad b. ʿUmayr b. Maḥfūẓ al-Balawī, Abū Muḥammad, al-Miṣrī.

chunks.arabic_text: كَذَّابٌ، وَضَّاعٌ لِلْحَدِيثِ، لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَى حَدِيثِهِ، وَلَا يُعْبَأُ بِهِ.

translations.en: A liar, a fabricator of ḥadīths, his ḥadīths are not turned to, and he is insignificant.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* characterizes ʿAbdullāh al-Balawī as a *kadhdhāb* (liar) whose hadith are largely disregarded (*lā yulfaṭu ilā ḥadīhi*), reflecting the rigorous scrutiny of narrators in Shia hadith sciences. His status as a fabricator underscores the importance of *ʿadāla* (integrity) and *ḍabṭ* (precision) in validating religious traditions, particularly in distinguishing authentic reports from those influenced by personal bias or error.
en.seo_question: Who is ʿAbdullāh al-Balawī and what is his status in hadith sciences?
